proposal.recommendation: The plan clears the buffer in both the P50 and P10 cases
proposal.recommendation_detail: Four levers, ranked by cost per dollar of relief. The terms negotiation is free and permanent but uncertain; the PO delay is free and certain but borrows cover; clearance and credit both cost real money. Every number here is computed by the story that owns the consequence.

slate.title: Delay two POs by one week
slate.body: Two of the six week-7 POs are for Core SKUs at 31 and 34 days of cover. Moving them into week 8 puts the outflow after the Amazon settlement lands.
slate.consequence: Cover on four SKUs drops to 24 days at the point of the delay, which is inside the Core service-level floor of 95% but not comfortable. Priced through the replenishment engine: 96.1% projected service level, no Hero SKU affected, no stock-out risk inside the window.
slate.sizeNote: Cover 24 days on four SKUs. Service level 96.1%, above the 95% floor.

slate.title: Negotiate Kessler to Net 60
slate.body: Kessler is mid-negotiation on their price notice and the terms ask is already on the brief. Net 45 to Net 60 moves the $88K PO out of week 7 entirely.
slate.consequence: This is the only lever that costs nothing and improves DPO permanently — 15 days of terms is worth $31K of working capital every cycle, not just this one. The risk is that it is a negotiation, not a decision: Kessler can say no, and the answer will not be known until Oct 4.

slate.title: Accelerate the clearance ladder
slate.body: Pull the first two ladder steps forward from week 9 to week 6, bringing recovery cash in ahead of the trough rather than after it.
slate.consequence: Deeper discounts earlier means lower total recovery: the same units clear at 61% of landed cost instead of 68%. That is real margin given up to buy timing — and it is only worth it if the timing is what actually matters.
slate.sizeNote: Recovery 65% instead of 68%. Modest, and the cohort still clears before the fee cliff.

slate.title: Draw the revolving line
slate.body: The cheapest facility, three business days to draw, no covenant tested below 60% utilisation. Available at any size in $25K increments.
slate.consequence: Straightforward and priced to the dollar — but it treats a timing problem as a funding problem. Drawn for 21 days it costs interest and nothing else; drawn as a habit it becomes the reason the conversion cycle never gets fixed.
slate.sizeNote: 21 days outstanding at 9.4% — $410 of interest. Closes most of the P50 gap alone.
